newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers, union sign two-yr wage agreement.
newsitem.headline: De Beers, union sign two-yr wage agreement.

text.p: De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd said on Thursday it and South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers had concluded annual wage talks with the signing of a two-year agreement.
De Beers said the agreement was the first such agreement in the South African mining industry.
In terms of the agreeement the monthly pensionable rates of pay for employees in the bargaining unit are increased by 9.7 percent with effect from July 1.
The parties have also agreed to increase the minimum wage to 1,639 rand through the abolition from August of the A1 sub-grade.
From May 1998 salaries will increase by the official April 1997 to April 1998 Consumer Price Index (CPI) as published by the Central Statistical Service.

De Beers and the NUM have committed themselves to finalise a formal agreement for the implementation of a merit award system by January 1998 across all divisions, with the exception of Venetia Mines where such a scheme has been in effect for a number of years.
De Beers said that employees in the A1 sub-grade would be trained to perform A2 tasks. Employees would also receive a one percent service increment.
On June 23 De Beers and Namdeb Diamond Corp agreed a two-year wage deal with the Mineworkers Union of Namibia (MUN).
